Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. quietus.title: Kraftwerk Berlin Issues Apology After Hosting Military AI Event
quietus.description: The Berlin venue's head of sales, Tjabo Reuter, has described it as "a serious error of judgement" Kraftwerk Berlin, the venue that hosts Berlin Atonal and houses clubs such as Tresor and OHM within its complex, has apologied after it hosted an event for German defence technology company Helsing last week. The event on 11 November saw Helsing launch Clarity, its new AI-supported military intelligence platform, in Kraftwerk's main Turbine Hall. Helsing has hit the headlines in recent years after Spotify co-founder and former CEO Daniel Ek emerged as a key investor in the business. Kraftwerk Berlin's head of sales, Tjabo Reuter, has now apologised for allowing the space to be used by Helsing…

quietus.title: Inner Rebellion: Lorenzo Senni Interviewed
quietus.description: Ahead of the release of his latest album for Warp Records, All Ages, the Italian artist discusses the skateboarding and hardcore music culture that inspired him as a teenager, and the act of rebellion he took against himself in making the new LP Photo by Jim C. Nedd With a population of around 1,000 people, Lorenzo Senni’s childhood village of Ronta wasn’t especially a thriving hub for cultural activity when he was growing up. While it wasn’t far from the more active nearby cities of Cesena and Rimini, where he occasionally visited as an impressionable teen, its leisurely way of living made for a generation of young people desperate to find new hobbies and something out of the ordinary.…

quietus.title: New River Studio Juan Atkins Tribute on Friday Night
quietus.description: A film screening & three DJ sets have been planned to memorialise the "incredibly important" Michigan artist Juan Atkins – techno's 'The Originator' who died at the end of last month – is being memorialised at an event held at New River Studios, Harringay on Friday night. As well as DJ sets from tQ favourites UKAEA, Ruby Quick and Proteus, there will be a screening of the documentary The Last Angel Of History. John Akomfrah and Eddie George's documentary feature is a comment on and narrative thread in Afrofuturism, which, among many other things, encompasses Detroit techno. Organiser / DJ Proteus says: "[He was] The Originator – Juan Atkins was more than an artist, [he was] an unstoppable…

quietus.title: Worlds Apart: Noon by Richard Skelton & Lawrence English
quietus.description: Two deep listeners, Room 40 records boss English and Lancashire-born composer Skelton, find a still point in the midst of the storm of contemporary history on their new collaborative album credit Richard Skelton & Lawrence English For two people standing on opposite sides of the planet, one’s midday becomes the other’s midnight. This first collaboration between British musician Richard Skelton and Australian composer Lawrence English hinges on the duality of this proposition: Skelton’s name written upside down beneath English’s, both pressed against the album cover’s featureless greyness, while the brightness of the palindrome NOON drowns in the supreme darkness of their music. NOON…

quietus.title: Organic Intelligence LXII: C64 Game Soundtracks
quietus.description: In this month’s antidote to the algorithm, Juliet Jacques explores the playful and experimental soundtracks to games on the popular tape-based home computer I spent my first year at the University of Manchester in halls of residence. They put me in with a group of lads who were really into techno, and drum and bass – a challenge to my sensibilities, as I had a tribal allegiance to punk, post-punk and independent music. During our first weeks together, in September 2000, a single came out that instantly became a massive hit but united my flatmates in disgust: ‘Kernkraft 400’ by Zombie Nation. I immediately recognised the hook – “it’s from a Commodore 64 game”, I told them. “I bet it…

quietus.title: Maria Teresa Pirrigheddu and Vieri Mura – Rundinas
quietus.description: Maria Teresa Pirrigheddu and Vieri Mura Rundinas An album of Sardinian cantu a chiterra proves softly spoken but full of character Rundinas by Maria Teresa Pirrigheddu & Vieri Mura The path to Rundinas, a collection of songs in the cantu a chiterra style of northern Sardinia, began with a research project. Vieri Mura, an Italian musician, composer and researcher of Sardinian heritage, interviewed Maria Teresa Pirrigheddu, a known singer of cantu a chiterra, as part of an ethnography of Sardinian music. The friendship that followed from these meetings eventually produced Rundinas (‘swallows’, like the birds that return to Sardinia), with lyrics pulled from Pirrigheddu’s favourite…

quietus.title: Glastonbury Reveals First Acts for 2027 Edition
quietus.description: Massive Attack, Kraftwerk and Cher are among the big names heading to the Somerset farm next summer Glastonbury has revealed the first wave of acts playing its 2027 edition. The festival will be headlined by Billie Eilish, Harry Styles and Sam Fender, while Cher will take the Sunday afternoon 'Legends slot' at the main Pyramid stage. Also high up on the bill are Massive Attack, Kraftwerk, The xx, Little Simz and Ezra Collective. The first lineup announcement is rounded out by the likes of FKA twigs, Robyn, Primal Scream, Underworld, De La Soul, The Avalanches, Dinosaur Jr., underscores, Hot Chip, Mike D, Young Fathers and Thundercat. Next year's Glastonbury marks the first edition of the…

quietus.title: The Strange World Of… The New Blockaders
quietus.description: Nick Soulsby, author of a new book charting TNB's bizarre 45-year journey, selects ten points of entry into the maze-like discography of a group dedicated to absurdity and the refusal of fixed meaning TNB at Cafe Oto in 2017, by Baby RL At the tail-end of the 70s, artists in the non-academic realm joined illustrious composers of electroacoustic and experimental music in probing where the outer limits of music might lie, and the extent to which its core characteristics could be twisted to unleash new sounds. Magnetic tape and fanzine culture alike inspired a wider web of individuals with no industry-backing, no money, no audience, and no media connections to create, then to share their work…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Trio Ternura :: A Gira / Razão De Ser
aquariumdrunkard.description: Trio Ternura—the Brazilian sibling group consisting of sisters Jussara and Jurema and brother Robson Ternura—has been receiving the reissue treatment via Madrid’s Vampisoul label since last year and we are absolutely here for it. Last year, they dished out a new pressing of the group’s 1973 single “A Gira” b/w “Last Tango in Paris.” The A-side is a polyrhythmic groove with tribal percussion and silky, chanting harmonies which finds itself paired with a glittery lounge rendering of Argentinean saxophonist Gato Barbieri’s Grammy-winning film score.

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Aquarium Drunkard Show: SIRIUS/XMU (7pm PST, Channel 35)
aquariumdrunkard.description: A ramble through the Antipodean underground and beyond. Broadcasting from northeast Los Angeles — the Aquarium Drunkard Show on SIRIUS/XMU, channel 35. 7pm California time, Wednesdays. 34.1090° N, 118.2334° W

aquariumdrunkard.title: Transmissions :: Larry Crane (Tape Op)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Today on Transmissions, a conversation with Larry Crane of Tape Op magazine. This year, Larry and Tape Op celebrated 30 years of creative advice with Making Music , a book that collects 26 of the best ever interviews from the magazine, including creators like Glyn Johns, Tony Visconti, RZA, Brian Eno, Joe Boyd, Lee “Scratch” Perry, and many more. It’s not just for recording aficionados, but it never skimps on glorious detail.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Sterlin Harjo :: The Aquarium Drunkard Interview
aquariumdrunkard.description: FX’s The Lowdown , which stars Ethan Hawke as an investigative journalist and self-professed "truthstorian," isn’t trying to hide anything from studio executives or its audience. The Lowdown is a hilarious, lovingly shambolic, shaggy dog crime show. It’s dazzling and comprehensive musical selection is led by the show’s creator/executive producer/writer/director Sterlin Harjo. The filmmaker—who is Seminole/Muscogee, grew up in Oklahoma, and currently lives in Tulsa—joins us to discuss the show's unique sound.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Ben Webster :: Music For Loving (1955)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Music for Loving (1955) contains some of Ben Webster’s most sophisticated and elegant work, and the larger arrangements avoid the pitfalls of the “jazz-with-strings” genre. This is none more apparent than when the orchestral bells and whistles step aside, allowing Webster and his band the space to linger in the crestfallen ballads.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Inspiration, Not Limitation :: The Residents’ Eskimo Journey
aquariumdrunkard.description: Many people have seen the Residents, but few know what their members actually look like. The group has maintained anonymity for over 50 years, through hundreds of releases, concerts, books, films, and pretty much every other kind of media. Still, if you've heard of them, you probably know their signature look: tuxedo with top hat perched upon a helmet that resembles a big, veiny eyeball. But did you know the eyeball wasn't always part of the Residents story?

aquariumdrunkard.title: Bob Dylan :: The Rolling Thunder Revue: The 1976 Live Recordings
aquariumdrunkard.description: We all need a hobby. Some people get into fantasy football. Others are obsessed with knitting. There’s cosplay, astronomy, astrology, ham radio … the possibilities are endless. But for my money, the best hobby a guy or gal can have is Bob Dylan. The man just continues to give, even as he cruises through his mid-eighties.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Lotti Tauber :: Concern and Simplicity Volume 1: Original Recordings, 1981–1986
aquariumdrunkard.description: Yet another stunning archival find from the Freedom to Spend label?! Every time this crew pops up, you ask yourself how they’ve somehow unearthed more astounding and unique gems from the past. But FT$ has that magic touch. Case in point: Concern and Simplicity Volume 1: Original Recordings, 1981–1986 , Freedom to Spend’s latest release. Made up of barely circulated material by the late Swiss pianist / composer Lottie Tauber, it’s a minimalist marvel, influenced by Satie, Glass and the I-Ching.

mubi.title: The Last Emperor: A Conversation with Jeremy Thomas
mubi.description: The Last Emperor (Bernardo Bertolucci, 1987). When Jeremy Thomas died on September 11, 2026, the British film industry lost a titan. A producer who paid no heed to the vagaries of popular culture, Thomas was led by his impeccable palate for cinematic ambition, unswayed by whether audiences or critics came along for the ride. A list of filmmakers whose work makes up Thomas’s production portfolio reads like a who’s who of maverick visionaries, each of them fiercely loyal to the last: Nicolas Roeg and David Cronenberg; Takeshi Kitano and Jonathan Glazer; Nagisa Ōshima and Wim Wenders; Jerzy Skolimowski and Bernardo Bertolucci, whose The Last Emperor (1987) won Thomas the Academy Award for…
